Formula Joining adjacent regions a and b raises the within-region sum of squares by dW = n_a n_b / (n_a + n_b) * sum over columns c of (mean_ac - mean_bc)^2. The contracted graph computes this cost once per unique adjacent region pair and reuses it until either region changes. Every tract starts alone with W = 0 and each merge adds its dW, so the final W is the exact within-region sum of squares (standardized units unless standardize is false). sequential merges the cheapest adjacent pair per iteration; mutual-nearest merges every mutually cheapest pair per round, restricted to the remaining target budget, and can stop at a different partition.
